newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline unions call November 27/28 strike.
newsitem.headline: French airline unions call November 27/28 strike.

text.p: Trade unions plan to strike at Air France and other French airlines on November 27 and 28 and are due to meet transport minister Bernard Pons on Monday night for talks on their grievances, a CFDT union official said.
"It is time for all air transport staff to mobilise against provocation by the public authorities and the management of Air France," a CFDT statement said.
The CFDT official contacted by Reuters said the decision to strike was taken last week by several unions representing pilots and steward staff and would concern all French airlines.
But he said it was still possible the strike could be called off if the meeting with Pons made enough progress.
"It can always be called off," the official said.
Pilots unions at Air France Europe, a short-haul unit of the Air France group, had already said on November 14 that they planned to strike on November 27 and 28.

An Air France spokeswoman, contacted by Reuters on Monday, said the group was not in a position to measure the likely impact of the strike on the grounds that it "did not know the precise list of the unions calling for the strike".
The SNPL union confirmed the strike dates and that the action concerned all French airlines.
Unions are protesting against sub-contracting and are seeking a reduction in work time among other grievances.
